description: wsHttpBinding service with typed faults, Windows message security, nullable/default values, decimal/date/enum semantics, and KnownType polymorphism.

facts.claim: GetInvoice declares ValidationFault as a typed FaultContract.
The wsHttpBinding uses SOAP message security and Windows credentials.

endpoints.security: SOAP message security, Windows credentials, secure conversation

risks.consequence: The fault code, reason, detail, and client catch behavior require an explicit gRPC status and error-details contract.

risks.construct: wsHttpBinding message security with Windows secure conversation
risks.consequence: SOAP message security has no direct gRPC equivalent; transport security, identity propagation, and authorization must be redesigned.
Proto presence, decimal precision, timestamp rules, unknown enum handling, and polymorphic shape must be specified and tested.

questions.prompt: Which identity and authorization model replaces Windows SOAP message security?
Is the PaymentMethod subtype set closed, and must unknown future subtypes round-trip?
questions.trigger: KnownType-based inheritance is used on a contract field.

rpcs.notes: Map validation failures to INVALID_ARGUMENT plus a versioned ValidationError detail.

typeMappings.notes: Use explicit presence, a lossless DecimalValue, UTC Timestamp policy, UNSPECIFIED enum zero, and oneof for payment subtypes.
Use google.rpc.Status-compatible error details and preserve machine-readable field violations.

workPackages.objective: Specify invoice messages, presence, decimal, timestamp, enum, oneof, and error details.
Implement TLS, replacement authentication, authorization policies, and identity propagation.
Implement the ASP.NET Core gRPC adapter and parity tests for success, faults, and serialization edges.

expectations: The target remains gRPC on ASP.NET Core; SOAP message security is recorded as a blocking redesign risk.
Golden parity cases cover null versus default, high-precision decimal, leap-day UTC timestamps, unknown enums, every KnownType subtype, and typed validation faults.
